excerpt: E. G. Paddock will immediately begin the erection of a first-class livery stable, 38x50 feet.

title: Jennie Wilkes's poem printed
summary: The Cow Boy printed the poem "Good Bye" by Jennie Wilkes, with an editor's note praising the young author's ability.
excerpt: For one so young, it shows superior poetical ability.—Ed.]

title: Snow over a foot deep; cattle losses may reach five per cent
summary: Snow lay more than a foot deep on the level, the heaviest fall in the memory of the oldest inhabitant; the paper estimated cattle losses at up to five per cent.
excerpt: The snow is over a foot deep on the level, a heavier fall than there has been within the memory of the oldest inhabitant.

title: O. H. Holt publishes pamphlet on Dakota
summary: Gov. Pierce's private secretary O. H. Holt published a pamphlet on Dakota's resources that included an extract written by the Cow Boy's editor; Packard recommended it while doubting his own tenderfoot claim that cattle paw snow away to reach grass.
excerpt: One of the extracts written by the editor of the Cow Boy in his tenderfoot days contains the information that cattle paw away the snow
people: O. H. Holt; A. T. Packard

title: Lloyd Roberts contracts 400 cattle for Glendive
summary: Lloyd Roberts contracted to deliver 400 head of cattle to Glendive, to the same firm he supplied the year before.
excerpt: Lloyd Roberts has already made a contract to deliver four hundred head of cattle to Glendive.

title: Dan Friedman reports cheap cattle in Minnesota
summary: A letter from Dan Friedman, Lloyd Roberts' cattle-buying partner, at Cold Spring, Minn., reported yearlings at $9-10 and two-year-olds at $14-16.
excerpt: cattle there are at the lowest notch, nine to ten dollars for yearlings and fourteen to sixteen for two-year-olds.

title: Ex-sheriff Belding of Deadwood goes home
summary: Ex-sheriff Belding of Deadwood, "speaker of the third house at Bismarck," went home on Friday's coach.
excerpt: Ex-sheriff Belding, of Deadwood, and speaker of the third house at Bismarck, went home on last Friday's coach.

title: George Wilkes buys slaughter-house machinery in Chicago
summary: George Wilkes returned from Chicago having bought nearly $8,000 of machinery, including Buckeye-pattern boilers, for the new slaughter house.
excerpt: the total cost in Chicago amounting to nearly $8,000.

title: Dance planned at the Metropolitan hotel
summary: George Fitzgerald planned a dance, open to all, to open his Metropolitan hotel.
excerpt: A week from next Saturday Mr. Fitzgerald will give a dance to which all are cordially invited.

title: Wells-Fargo route agent visits Cow Boy office

excerpt: Mr. Stebbins, route agent for the Wells-Fargo Ex. Co., made us a visit last Saturday.

title: Rise of water reported coming down the Little Missouri
summary: With the weather below zero, word came that a rise of three or four feet of water was coming down the river, then about 25 miles upstream and travelling four or five miles a day; it was expected at Medora on the 26th or 27th.
excerpt: word came that there was a raise of three or four feet of water coming, and at that time was about twenty-five miles up the river.

title: Wife of Dakota's delegate to Congress buried

people: Mrs. J. B. Raymond; J. B. Raymond

summary: Rev. Mr. Scheffner of Dickinson came down expecting to preach, but no arrangements had been made and the meeting was postponed.

title: Colemans celebrate eighteenth wedding anniversary
summary: M. M. and Mrs. Coleman celebrated their eighteenth wedding anniversary with a large gathering of friends.
excerpt: M. M. and Mrs. Coleman celebrated their eighteenth wedding anniversary, the evening of the twenty-second.

title: Judge Church leaves for the Black Hills by coach
summary: Judge Church of Deadwood took Monday morning's coach for the Hills.
excerpt: Judge Church, of Deadwood, was a passenger for the Hills on Monday morning's coach.

title: Scaffolding collapse injures Thos. Dudgeon at slaughter-house

excerpt: A scaffolding broke on the slaughter-house, Monday, and severely injured Thos. Dudgeon.

title: Father Martin celebrates Mass in Medora
summary: Father Martin came from Mandan to celebrate Mass on Tuesday morning.
excerpt: Mass was celebrated Tuesday morning by Father Martin, who came from Mandan for that purpose.

title: Next Medora Gun Club meeting called
summary: The gun club's next meeting was set for the same place the following Wednesday evening, and all wishing to join were urged to attend.
excerpt: The next meeting of the club will be held at the same place on next Wednesday evening

title: J. B. Walker goes to Mandan to outfit the Pyramid Park hotel
summary: J. B. Walker went to Mandan to purchase an outfit for the Pyramid Park hotel.
excerpt: J. B. Walker went to Mandan yesterday morning to purchase an outfit for the Pyramid Park hotel.

title: Johnny Kiefer returns from the East
summary: Johnny Kiefer returned from his eastern trip and reported his wife almost entirely recovered.
excerpt: Johnny Kiefer returned last night from his eastern trip.

title: Dr. H. M. Jorgens and family settle in Medora
summary: Dr. H. M. Jorgens, his wife and sons arrived on the coach from Cave Hills and began housekeeping; the doctor was considering putting in a herd of cattle.
excerpt: Dr. H. M. Jorgens, wife and sons came in on yesterday morning's coach from Cave Hills.

title: Bad Lands Gun Club organized
summary: The Bad Lands Gun Club adopted its constitution, providing for weekly Saturday rifle, shotgun and revolver contests; A. T. Packard, E. G. Paddock and J. N. Maxwell formed the executive committee.
excerpt: The following is the constitution of the Gun club as adopted last evening.
people: A. T. Packard; E. G. Paddock; J. N. Maxwell

title: Warm weather and chinook wind end hard winter spell
summary: Warm weather began on the 25th and a chinook wind set in on the morning of the 26th, expected to clear the snow within two days, to the relief of cattlemen facing heavier than usual losses.
excerpt: A regular chinook wind set in early this morning and two more days will completely clear the ground of snow.

title: Frank Walker badly wounded by accidental rifle discharge
summary: Frank Walker's leg was shattered below the knee when a loaded rifle lying on a chair discharged; Dr. Robart was trying to save the leg. An editorial called careless handling of fire-arms criminal.
excerpt: The ball entered the leg just below the knee and shattered both bones.

title: Jim Butler to build E. G. Paddock's livery stable
summary: Jim Butler would begin building E. G. Paddock's livery stable after finishing the skating rink.
excerpt: Jim. Butler will begin the erection of E. G. Paddock's livery stable as soon as he finishes the skating rink.

title: Little Missouri high; top ice breaking
summary: The river was high and the top ice breaking, though the bottom ice was not expected to go out soon.
excerpt: The river is up high and the top ice is breaking.

title: Ayers and Maxwell go east; W. H. Ladd fills in as agent
summary: Messrs. Ayers and Maxwell left on a pleasure trip east of a week or two; W. H. Ladd took Maxwell's place in his absence.
excerpt: Messrs. Ayers and Maxwell have gone east on a pleasure trip of a week or two.
people: Ayers; J. N. Maxwell; W. H. Ladd

title: Foundations laid under the hotel de Mores
summary: Most of the foundations had been laid under the hotel de Mores and the partitions knocked out, with work to resume when the weather settled.
excerpt: Most of the foundations have been laid under the hotel de Mores

title: Cowboys arrested for delaying the train at Mingusville
summary: Cowboys who delayed a train at Mingusville in a drunken spree faced federal charges for obstructing the mail; several had been arrested and taken to Helena.
excerpt: A number of them have already been arrested and taken to Helena.

title: Dr. J. J. Clemmer of the Cave Hills buys imported Aberdeen-Angus
summary: Dr. J. J. Clemmer of Clemmer & Dell, Cave Hills, wrote from Cresco, Iowa, endorsing Aberdeen-Angus and reported buying six imported head at $400 each.
excerpt: Dr. Clemmer recently purchased six head of imported Aberdeen-Angus at a cost of four hundred dollars a head.

title: Grand jury may investigate the Marquis de Morès over the Luffsey shooting
summary: Quoting the Mandan Pioneer, the paper reported that a coming grand jury was expected to investigate the charge that the Marquis de Morès shot the hunter Luffsey at Little Missouri; Justices Bateman and Collins had earlier acquitted him.
excerpt: the grand jury will be called upon, at its forthcoming meeting, to investigate the charge against the Marquis de Mores of shooting the hunter Luffsey.

title: Howard Eaton in St. Paul on business
summary: Howard Eaton was in St. Paul on business and expected back in a few days.
excerpt: Howard Eaton is in St. Paul on business.

title: First Gun Club contest scheduled
summary: The Gun Club's first contest was set for 1:30 Saturday afternoon.
excerpt: All who wish to shoot must be on hand promptly at 1:30 Saturday afternoon as the contest will begin on time

title: Bad Lands Gun Club holds first shoot; Paddock wins
summary: The Bad Lands Gun Club held the first of five rifle contests; E. G. Paddock won with 55 of a possible 75, and A. T. Packard was second with 52.
excerpt: Mr. E. G. Paddock was the winner of the contest with a score of fifty-five out of a possible seventy-five.
people: E. G. Paddock; A. T. Packard

title: Daily stage service to the Hills promised for spring
summary: The paper said a daily stage to the Hills would be put on in the spring at least, or as soon as required, and predicted a railroad from Medora to the Hills.
excerpt: a daily will be put on in the spring at least.

title: Bishop expected to dedicate Medora Catholic church
summary: The bishop was expected to dedicate the church early in spring.
excerpt: It is expected that the bishop will be here to dedicate the church early next spring.

title: More cattle companies expected near Medora
summary: The paper was assured that several more large cattle companies intended to open ranches near Medora the next spring.
excerpt: several more large cattle companies intend opening ranches near Medora next spring.

title: New Medora roller rink expected to open
summary: Lumber for the new roller rink had been ordered, and the proprietors said the rink would be running about March 1. Rubber-wheeled skates were under discussion.
excerpt: the rink will be in running order about march 1st.

title: Pyramid Park hotel to change hosts
summary: Arch. Boyd planned to leave the Pyramid Park hotel on March 1, with J. B. Walker taking his place as host; Boyd would remain in the community.
excerpt: Arch. Boyd intends leaving the Pyramid Park hotel the first of March and J. B. Walker will take his place as host.

title: March 1885 weather at Medora
summary: T. Martin's record gave a mean 6 a.m. temperature of 27 degrees, coldest day March 16, warmest March 31, 3 inches of snowfall and mostly northwest winds.
excerpt: Coldest day .... Mar. 16. Warmest day .. Mar. 31.

title: Three bighorn ewes killed and sold in town
summary: Three bighorn ewes, each said to carry two lambs, were brought into town and sold; the paper called for enforcement of Dakota game laws.
excerpt: three big-horn sheep, all ewes, were brought into town and sold.

title: Willis Eaton arrives in Medora
summary: Willis Eaton arrived Monday.
excerpt: Willis Eaton descended on us like a wolf on the fold Monday.

title: Baby born to the Garver family
summary: A doctor came from Dickinson on Tuesday for the birth of a baby to Mrs. Garver; her mother, Mrs. Nichols of Bismarck, was attending her.
excerpt: The Doctor came up from Dickinson Tuesday and brought a little red baby
people: Georgie Garver; Mrs. Garver; Mrs. Nichols

title: Capital removal bill revived in territorial house; bribery charged
summary: The house revived the bill moving the capital to Pierre, 25 to 23, and Mark Ward charged W. S. Wells and V. P. Prentice of Pierre with corrupt offers.
excerpt: No sooner had the vote been announced than a bombshell was fired into the ranks of the South Dakotians
people: Mark Ward; W. S. Wells; V. P. Prentice

title: Sergent Smith of Fort Meade passes through on the coach
summary: Sergent Smith of Fort Meade came up on the Wednesday coach and left for Fort Keogh.
excerpt: Sergent Smith, of Fort Meade, came up on Wednesday's coach and left for Ft. Keogh.

title: Frank Walker's leg amputated
summary: Dr. Robart of Dickinson amputated Frank Walker's leg, shattered in an accident reported the week before; Walker was resting easily and expected on crutches in three or four weeks.
excerpt: It was found necessary yesterday morning to amputate the leg, the amputation being preformed by the attending physician, Dr. Robart.

title: Raffle for Frank Walker's rifle raises money for his bills
summary: A raffle of Frank Walker's rifle, belt and knife sold 124 chances after Johnny Munro canvassed the town; Frank Katela won, and the proceeds went toward Walker's bills. W. B. Wright had given $50 earlier.
excerpt: A hundred and twenty-four chances were sold and the outfit was finally won by Frank Katela.
people: Frank Walker; Johnny Munro; Frank Katela; W. B. Wright

title: "Cold Turkey Bill" in from North Grand stage station
summary: "Cold Turkey Bill" came in from the North Grand stage station on Wednesday.
excerpt: "Cold Turkey Bill" came in from North Grand stage station, Wednesday

title: Vic Smith leaves on a beaver-hunting trip down the Missouri
summary: Vic Smith left for a point above Fort Buford to buy a skiff and float down the Missouri shooting beaver at the spring break-up.
excerpt: He started last night for a point several hundred miles above Fort Buford

title: Bad Lands Cattle Co. reports light winter losses
summary: M. Wadsworth, manager of the Bad Lands Cattle Co., said fewer dead cattle of his brands had been found than could be counted on one's fingers among some 3,000 head.
excerpt: the finding of less dead cattle of his brands than can be counted on one's fingers.

title: Vic Smith's beaver-hunting trip down the Missouri
summary: Vic Smith left Medora March 4, traveled by Glendive, Wolf Point and Ft. Galpin to Milk river, trapped beaver, and after the river broke on March 26 floated down by skiff to Bismarck with about $300 in beaver skins.
excerpt: He started from Medora March 4th and reached Glendive
places: Medora; Glendive; Wolf Point; Milk river; Bismarck

title: Medora school term closes
summary: School closed for the term, with another term likely to be arranged.
excerpt: School closes this week.

title: Spring building boom expected in Medora
summary: The Cow Boy predicted that many buildings would be erected and new businesses established in Medora that spring.
excerpt: Many buildings will be erected and new businesses will be established.

title: The Marquis expected home
summary: The Marquis de Morès was expected home on the night train.
excerpt: The Marquis is expected home on to-night's train.

title: Territorial council passes capital removal bill 14 to 10
summary: The council passed the bill relocating the capital at Pierre, removal not before May 18, 1886; a veto was expected.
excerpt: The bill was then put on its final passage and carried by a vote of 14 to 10.

title: Son born to the Marquise de Morès
summary: A healthy boy was born to the Marquise de Morès; both were doing well.
excerpt: The news arrived too late for our last issue that a healthy boy baby was born to the Marquise de Mores. Both are doing finely and we wish a long life to the future heir.
people: Marquise de Morès; Marquis de Morès

title: Pipe and fittings arrive for night tanking work
summary: Two car loads of pipe and fittings arrived, boilers were expected, and a Winnipeg engineer was coming to take charge of tanking.
excerpt: Two car loads of pipe and fittings have arrived and the boilers are expected daily. An assistant engineer will soon arrive from Winnipeg, who will take charge of the tanking, which will all be done at night.

title: Slaughter-house construction nears completion
summary: The slaughter-house would be done in about three weeks; Peter Book holds the contract for an 85-foot smoke stack.
excerpt: The slaughter-house will be finished in about three weeks. Owing to the change in the plans, the roof will be raised four feet. Peter Book has the contract for the smoke stack, which will be eighty five feet high, with a twenty foot base.

title: Roller rink opens with ball and regular hours
summary: The skating rink's opening ball was a success and regular evening and ladies' hours were announced; J. C. Fisher and E. Deffebach run it.
excerpt: The opening ball of the skating rink was a complete success. About twelve sets were danced and then the skating began. The floor was pronounced very satisfactory and all enjoyed themselves to the utmost. The craze has struck Medora and every one who has not learned is going to try the "little wagons." Messrs. Fisher and Deffebach were much pleased with the attendance and a maple floor will be the next thing on the programme.

title: Medora building boom continues
summary: The sound of hammers had been heard in Medora for five months, with several new buildings coming and demand for store rooms.
excerpt: There hasn't been a minute during working hours for five months that the sound of hammers has not been heard in Medora. Fram the present prospect it would seem that the same sound will continue all summer. Several new buildings will be put up immediately and others will come later. The best of it is that no useless ones are erected and there is pressing demand for store rooms now.

title: Medora Stage and Forwarding Co. restricts employee contracts
summary: A notice signed by the Marquis de Morès as president said company bills are void unless approved by Treasurer W. F. Van Driesche.
excerpt: Notice is hereby given that any contracts or bills made by any of the employes of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co., will not be paid or recognized unless approved by W. F. Van
people: Marquis de Morès; W. F. Van Driesche

title: B. Barr's Texas herd likely delayed by quarantine
summary: B. Barr, in Kansas City, expected a Texas herd this summer but quarantine laws will probably make him put it off.
excerpt: B. Barr is in Kansas City doing a good business. He expected to have a herd of Texans here this summer but the quarantine laws will probably oblige him to put it off.

title: Third avenue and Main street crossing graded
summary: A little grading improved the crossing of Third avenue and Main street in Medora.
excerpt: A little grading materially improved the appearance of the crossing of Third avenue and Main street.

title: Seaton letter on Jones & Pennell outfit published
summary: The paper printed a letter from Uncle John Seaton describing the Jones & Pennell outfit's winter trek from Lake Superior and new Croton Aqueduct tunnel work near Yonkers, N. Y.; their stock was shipped to Medora.
excerpt: Shipping our stock to Medora and ourselves to this point, we arrived on the 14th inst.
people: John Seaton; Joe Pennell; T. G. Jones; Howard Eaton

title: Hard winter on stock reported
summary: The paper reported an exceptionally hard winter on stock, with the Bad Lands suffering less than other areas because of lighter snowfall.
excerpt: Reports from all sections of the country both east and west show that this has been an exceptionally hard winter on stock.

title: Texas cattle drives expected to halt under quarantine laws
summary: The paper predicted no Texas cattle would be driven this season because of Kansas and Nebraska quarantine laws and fear of Texas fever.
excerpt: It is doubtful if any cattle will be driven from Texas this season.

title: Governor Pierce vetoes capital removal bill
summary: The paper praised Governor Pierce for vetoing the bill moving the capital from Bismarck, on legal grounds.
excerpt: He vetoed the bill and gave as a reason for his veto such legal reasons as are absolutely unanswerable.

title: Second gun club shoot set for Saturday
summary: The second shoot in the rifle series was set for Saturday at 1:30.
excerpt: The second shoot in the first series of five for the rifle comes off next Saturday at 1:30.

title: Bad Lands Gun Club holds second rifle shoot
summary: The second of five rifle shoots took place; Paddock led with Packard and Piper tied for second overall.
excerpt: The second shoot in the series of five for the rifle, took place last Saturday.
people: E. G. Paddock; A. T. Packard; Piper

title: Marquis de Morès arrives and travels over the stage line
summary: The Marquis came to Medora Sunday night, left Monday morning over the stage line and returned Wednesday.
excerpt: The Marquis came Sunday night and started Monday morning over the stage line. He returned yesterday.

title: Near accident behind the gun club target
summary: Brown narrowly escaped when Joe O'Brien fired at the butte while Brown was digging out bullets.
excerpt: It was a narrow escape and all should be careful about going behind the target

title: Bob Roberts ribbed as a New York dude
summary: Howard Eaton reported Bob Roberts passing as a dude in New York.
excerpt: If Howard Eaton hadn't told us we never would have belived it, but Bob Roberts was passing as a dude in New York. He had a plug hat, gold headed

title: Baby girl born to Mrs. Fitzgerald at the Metropolitan
summary: An eleven-pound girl was born to Mrs. Fitzgerald at the Metropolitan.
excerpt: Tuesday morning there was an arrival at the Metropolitan who departed from the usual rule and did not register. The arrival was a young lady and weighed eleven pounds. Mrs. Fitzgerald is the happy mother.

title: Ice gorge raises Little Missouri nearly five feet
summary: The river rose nearly five feet overnight, reaching the foundations of the new slaughter house.
excerpt: There must have been a large gorge down the river as the water raised nearly five feet night before last. It came up to the foundations of the new slaughter house and Dan Williams had to almost swim back after going out to see what the trouble was.

title: Vic Smith writes from Poplar Creek of heavy agency cattle losses
summary: The Cow Boy received a letter from Vic Smith dated March 10 at Poplar Creek saying cattle losses at the Wolf Point agency were heavy and the Indians were eating frozen beef, and that Medora was booming by comparison.
excerpt: He states that loss among the Wolf Point agency cattle is very heavy and that the Indians are living high on "frozen-to-death" beef.

title: Medora roller rink to open with a ball
summary: The new roller rink, to be managed by Mr. Deffebach, was to open the following Wednesday evening with a ball, with music from Glendive.
excerpt: The rink will be opened next Wednesday evening with a ball. Music from Glendive will be in attendance.

title: Father Martin celebrates mass at Medora
summary: Father Martin celebrated mass in the Catholic church.
excerpt: Father Martin celebrated mass in the Catholic church, yesterday morning.

title: J. W. Gallup comes from Cave Hills to become postmaster
summary: J. W. Gallup arrived by coach from Cave Hills to get his postmaster papers.
excerpt: J. W. Gallup came in on yesterday's coach from Cave Hills to get his papers made out as post master at that place. The post-office department has advertised for bids for carrying the mails from Medora to Deadwood, the contract to begin July 1.

title: George Wilkes captures a rare bat
summary: George Wilkes caught a large reddish bat at the slaughter house and will send it east for exhibition.
excerpt: George Wilkes captured a large bat last night at the slaughter house that is a curiosity. It is much larger than ordinary, is of a reddish color streaked with white and belongs to a very rare species. It is rather long in the body and is very heavy for its size. George will send it east for exhibition in a few days.

title: J. L. Truscott goes to Bismarck on stock business
summary: J. L. Truscott left for Bismarck on stock business.
excerpt: J. L. Truscott went to Bismarck this morning on stock business.

title: Johnny Goodall brings horses for the stage line
summary: Johnny Goodall returned from Bozeman with twenty horses for the stage line.
excerpt: Johnny Goodall returned from Bozeman this morning with twenty head of horses. They will be used on the stage line.

title: W. H. Merrifield goes east to buy cattle for the Maltese Cross outfit
summary: W. H. Merrifield of Ferris & Merrifield left for Minnesota and Iowa to buy a herd for the Maltese Cross outfit, returning about May 1. (The Maltese Cross was Theodore Roosevelt's ranch; Roosevelt is not named.)
excerpt: W. H. Merrifield, of Ferris & Merrifield, went east this morning to Minnesota and Iowa to buy a herd of cattle to be added to the Maltese cross outfit. He will return about the first of May.

title: Packard protests uncredited reprints of his "Chinook" sonnet
summary: The Cow Boy complained that its sonnet to "Chinook" was being reprinted by other papers and credited to anyone but the Cow Boy.
excerpt: They lighten the burden very materially, however, by crediting it to any other cattle paper in the country except the Cow Boy.

title: Abe Christopherson goes to Mingusville
summary: The Cow Boy reported that Abe Christopherson had gone to Mingusville.
excerpt: Abe Christopherson has gone to Mingusville.

title: "The Co." builds an additional barn
summary: The Cow Boy reported that "the Co." was building an additional barn south of the old one.
excerpt: The Co. is building an additional barn south of the old one.

title: Black Hills freight piles up at Medora
summary: The Cow Boy reported considerable Black Hills freight in the Medora freight house awaiting forwarding.
excerpt: There is considerable Black Hills fright in the freight house which will soon be forwarded.

title: Roads in poor condition
summary: The Cow Boy reported that roads were in poor condition everywhere and travel would be slow for a month or two.
excerpt: The roads are in poor condition everywhere and slow time will be made for a month or two.

summary: The Cow Boy reported that one of the broncos brought down by Johnny Goodall fell and was hurt so badly it had to be shot.

summary: The Cow Boy reported that John Wardenburg and his men had been painting the slaughter house and other buildings.

title: J. B. Walker praised for Pyramid Park hotel
summary: The Cow Boy praised J. B. Walker's management of the Pyramid Park hotel.
excerpt: J. B. Walker is running the Pyramid Park hotel up to a high standard of excellence.

title: George Wilkes' bat to go east for exhibition

excerpt: George Wilkes' bat is still alive and will soon be sent east for exhibition.

title: Mrs. Garver and Mrs. Fitzgerald ill
summary: The Cow Boy reported that Mrs. J. D. Garver and Mrs. Geo. Fitzgerald were both sick after overexertion following recent illness.

summary: The Cow Boy reported that constant high water and gradual melting had removed almost all chance of a Little Missouri flood.
excerpt: The constant high water and gradual melting of ice and snow takes away almost all chance of a flood of the Little Missouri.

excerpt: E. G. Paddock's livery stable is under weigh and will soon be completed.

title: Hotel de Mores remodeled
summary: The Cow Boy reported that work on the Hotel de Mores was progressing: rooms repartitioned, a new foundation, veneer and plaster, porches, and kitchen and laundry additions planned.
excerpt: Work is progressing favorably on the Hotel de Mores.

title: Postmaster Fisher ships joke "specimens"

title: John Warn waits for court in Bozeman
summary: The Cow Boy reported that John Warn was still in Bozeman waiting for court to sit.

title: A. Young finds lost mare dead in sink hole

excerpt: It had fallen into a sink hole about a hundred yards from his shack and smothered.

title: Bad Lands Cattle Co. finds few dead cattle
summary: The Cow Boy reported that a search found only two more dead cattle on the Bad Lands Cattle Co.'s range, eleven in all, suggesting winter losses close to natural levels.
excerpt: After diligent search only two more dead cattle have been found on the Bad Lands cattle Co's range, in addition to the nine already reported.

title: Spring well advanced on the Bad Lands range

title: Four weeks of perfect weather; rain wanted
summary: The paper reported four weeks of perfect weather around Medora but said the town was now wishing for rain; the grass was coming up but needed two or three days of rain.

excerpt: Miss Birdie Wadsworth has been quite sick for several days.

title: Medora short of eggs
summary: The Cow Boy suggested that someone could make a good living keeping the Medora market supplied with eggs.
excerpt: Some enterprising individual could make a good living by keeping the Medora market supplied with eggs.

title: George Myers bound over to circuit court; Ferris & Merrifield stand surety
summary: The Cow Boy reported that George Myers waived examination and was bound over in $1,000 bonds to the circuit court, with Ferris & Merrifield and Dantz as sureties, and predicted no grand jury would bring the case to trial.
excerpt: He is now bound over in $1,000 bonds to the circuit court, having waived examination. Ferris & Merrifield and Mm. Dantz are his sureties
people: George Myers; Sylvane Ferris; Bill Merrifield; Wm. Dantz

title: Packard closes out Studebaker wagon stock
summary: The Cow Boy carried A. T. Packard's notice that he would sell his stock of Studebaker wagons for cash below the wholesale factory rate to close them out.
excerpt: To close out the stock of Studebaker wagons now on hand, I will make prices for cash that are lower than the wholesale factory rate.

title: South Dakota 'state' legislature sits at Huron; Cow Boy opposes division
summary: The Cow Boy reported telegrams that the South Dakota statehood legislature in session at Huron would set its state government running, and argued that most Dakotans favored admission as one state and that the matter should go to a popular vote.
excerpt: Telegrams from Huron indicate that the state (?) legislature in session there will disregard the restraining clause in their constitution

title: Bob Roberts at Fort Steele
summary: The Cow Boy reported that Bob Roberts was at Ft. Steele.
excerpt: Bob. Roberts is at Ft. Steele.

title: Owenhouse makes otter-skin chaps for Howard Eaton
summary: The Cow Boy praised Bozeman saddler E. J. Owenhouse, saying he had recently made Howard Eaton the finest pair of chaps the paper had seen, out of otter skin.
excerpt: The finest pair of chapps we have ever seen, he made recently for Howard Eaton, out of otter skin.

title: Reports of plentiful deer
summary: The Cow Boy joked that reports suggested deer were so plentiful a poor hunter could kill one blindfolded with a club, but that they never came that way for the editor.
excerpt: a man must be a poor hunter who can't go out blind-folded and kill a deer with a club

title: Cow Boy office sells Huffman's round-up photographs
summary: The Cow Boy advertised remaining sets of Huffman's thirty-six instantaneous round-up photographs at $5, or $6 with a year's subscription, and recommended them to stockmen as Christmas presents.
excerpt: We have remaining a few sets of Huffmann's instantaneous round-up views, representing the most interesting events of the range cattle industry.

title: Mr. and Mrs. Arch Boyd leave Medora for Minot
summary: The Cow Boy reported that Mr. and Mrs. Arch. Boyd left Friday morning for Minot, the winter terminus of the Manitoba extension, undecided what they would do there.
excerpt: Minot has secured two good citizens at Medora's expense.

title: Maltese Cross cowboy George Myers brought back under arrest; Roosevelt and partners vouch for him
summary: The Cow Boy reported that George Myers, a hand at the Maltese Cross for several years, returned Sunday night with Fred Willard after his arrest on a Montana Stockgrowers' Association warrant for shipping two steers with the Maltese Cross cattle; the paper said the range's owners, Theodore Roosevelt and Ferris & Merrifield, all claimed Myers owned the cattle.
excerpt: As these gentlemen happen to be Theodore Roosevelt and Messrs, Ferris & Merrifield, and as they all claim that George owned the cattle
people: George Myers; Fred Willard; Theodore Roosevelt; Sylvane Ferris; Bill Merrifield
places: Medora; Maltese Cross Ranch; Garner Creek; Wooster, Ohio; Chicago

title: Alex. McKenzie of Bismarck visits Medora
summary: Alex. McKenzie of Bismarck spent several days in Medora.
excerpt: "Alex. McKenzie of Bismarck spent several days in Medora last week."

title: Light Chicago cattle receipts; northern range shipping season over
summary: The Cow Boy reported that only 7,000 cattle arrived at Chicago Monday, that state quarantines against Chicago slowed sales of feeders, and that the northern range shipping season had practically closed two weeks earlier.
excerpt: There were no northern rangers on the market, the season having practically closed for them two weeks ago.

title: J. C. Fisher leaves for Elyria, Ohio
summary: The Cow Boy reported that J. C. Fisher started Monday for Elyria, Ohio, to visit a month or six weeks before returning to Medora.
excerpt: J. C. Fisher started Monday for Elyria, Ohio

title: Chinook melts snow, then fresh snowfall
summary: The Cow Boy reported that a chinook on Monday night melted the snow very fast, but that about as much snow then fell to replace it.
excerpt: The chinook Monday night melted the snow very fast but as its force became spent, about as much snow fell to take the place of that melted.

title: Johnny McCadam leaves for Minneapolis
summary: The Cow Boy reported that Johnny McCadam left Tuesday morning for Minneapolis.
excerpt: Johnny McCadam left Tuesday morning for Minneapolis.

title: Dr. Heber Robarts passes through on east-bound train
summary: The Cow Boy reported that Dr. Heber Robarts, formerly of Dickinson and now of Hunters' Hot Springs, was on the east-bound train that morning.
excerpt: Dr. Heber Robarts, formerly of Dickinson and now of Hunters' Hot Springs was on the east-bound train this morning.

title: Northern Pacific cuts Dakota fares to four cents a mile
summary: The Northern Pacific reduced all passenger fares in Dakota to a uniform four cents a mile.
excerpt: "The Northern Pacific has reduced all passenger fares in Dakota to a uniform rate of four cents a mile."

title: Heavy holiday express traffic between Helena and Medora
summary: Express messengers were hard at work with holiday presents; one carried 201 way-bills between Helena and Medora.
excerpt: "One of them had 201 way-bills between Helena and Medora."

title: Billings County short of qualified officers
summary: The Cow Boy reported only two commissioners had qualified, one of them away in Texas, that new treasurer J. C. Fisher was on a six weeks' visit to Elyria, Ohio, and that no justice of the peace had qualified before the old terms expired Jan. 1; it urged commissioner Rowe to qualify.
excerpt: "It behooves Mr. Rowe, the third commissioner, to qualify at once and rescue us from our present \"slough of despond.\""
people: J. C. Fisher; W. F. Van Driesche; Mr. Rowe

title: John Norris opens restaurant in Coleman's building
summary: John Norris, formerly cook for Gill Kennedy, opened a restaurant in M. M. Coleman's building.
excerpt: "has opened a restaurant in M. M. Coleman's building."
people: John Norris; Gill Kennedy; M. M. Coleman

title: Chas. S. Eaton and family go to Mandan for the winter
summary: Chas. S. Eaton, his wife and his wife's mother went to Mandan for the winter and set up housekeeping.
excerpt: "will spend the winter in Mandn. They have already gone to housekeeping."

title: Overflow on river ice makes Little Missouri crossings nearly impassable
summary: Travelers using the river as a highway had difficulty at the crossings, with two to three feet of water on the old ice downriver.
excerpt: "the water is between two and three feet deep on the old ice"

title: Packard closes out his Studebaker wagon stock
summary: A. T. Packard offered his stock of Studebaker wagons below wholesale factory rates for cash to close out the stock on hand, and also offered wagon extras.
excerpt: "The only reason for making these rates is to close out stock on hand. They must and shall go soon."

title: Max Sanford of Dickinson expands holiday stock
summary: Max Sanford of Dickinson added $400 of silverware and other holiday goods and took mail orders by postal card.
excerpt: "Sanford, of Dickinson, has been adding largely to his stock"

title: Dr. Heber Roberts practising in Livingston
summary: Dr. Heber Roberts was reported practising in Livingston.
excerpt: "Dr. Heber Roberts is now practising in Livingston."

title: Cow Boy defends George Myers against cattle-theft charge
summary: Packard argued that Myers, who has worked several years for the Maltese Cross outfit owned by Theodore Roosevelt, is innocent, that the stockmen he has since spoken with scout the charge, and that the suit may cost Billings County taxpayers $1,500 or $2,000. He also accused Willard of a pleasure trip to Joliet, Ill., on the way to arrest Myers.
excerpt: "George Myers is now and for several years has been working for the Maltese Cross outfit, of which Ferris & Merrifield are managers and Theodore Roosevelt of New York is proprietor."
people: George Myers; Theodore Roosevelt; Sheriff Willard; A. T. Packard
tags: courts crime law press ranching tr

title: Theodore Roosevelt traveling in Europe with his bride
summary: The Cow Boy reported that Theodore Roosevelt was traveling in Europe with his bride and said his trip would be shortened by his coming to Medora to prove George Myers owned the two cattle.
excerpt: "Theodore Roosevelt is now traveling in Europe with his bride. His trip will be materially shortened by his coming here"

title: Warrants issued for Henry Williams and Jack Tisdale in Myers case
summary: Warrants were issued for the arrest of Henry Williams and Jack Tisdale as accessories in the case against George Myers; Williams was under bail.
excerpt: "Warrants have been issued for the arrest of Henry Williams and Jack Tisdale as accessories in the case against George Myers."
people: Henry Williams; Jack Tisdale; George Myers

title: Billings County tax case argued before Judge Francis at Bismarck
summary: The Billings County taxpayers' case against Stark County was argued all day; Judge Francis dissolved the preliminary injunction pro forma on an agreed case to go to the supreme court, with T. R. Selmes and Mr. Bullitt of St. Paul for Billings County.
excerpt: "Judge Francis rendered a pro forma decision that the preliminary injunction should be dissolved"
people: Judge Francis; T. R. Selmes; Mr. Flannery; Mr. Bullitt

title: Mike Seitz reaches Mandan with Capt. Cotton's horses
summary: Mike Seitz, who left the Logging Camp on December 10 with two of Capt. Cotton's horses, arrived in Mandan after a hard trip, making only ten miles the last day.
excerpt: "arrived in Mandan last Friday. The trip was a hard one, he only making ten miles the last day."

title: Sheriff Willard arrives in Bismarck from the west
summary: The Bismarck Tribune, as quoted, reported Sheriff Willard of Medora arrived from the west the day before.
excerpt: "Sheriff Willard of Medora, arrived from the west yesterday."

title: Bismarck Tribune attacks Packard over the Myers cattle case
summary: The Bismarck Tribune printed that Editor Packard had taken a stand against the stockmen in favor of George Myers, whom Sheriff Willard had brought back on a cattle-stealing charge. Packard reprinted both items and replied at length.
excerpt: "The fact that Editor Packard has taken a stand against the stockmen and in favor of Meyers, who was recently brought back for stealing cattle by Sheriff Willard"
people: A. T. Packard; Sheriff Willard; George Myers

title: Wrestling match at the Senate ends in a draw
summary: Jim Hayes and W. H. Wall wrestled at the Senate; each took a fall and the match was declared a draw.
excerpt: "A wrestling match came off at the Senate, Monday night, between Jim Hayes and W. H. Wall."

title: Mrs. James Foley and daughters return to Bismarck
summary: Mrs. James Foley and two daughters returned to Bismarck.
excerpt: "Mrs. James Foley and two daughters returned to Bismarck Tuesday morning."

title: Asylum superintendent appeals for Christmas gifts
summary: The Cow Boy printed a letter from O. W. Archibald, superintendent of the territorial insane asylum, asking friends across the territory to send money or articles for the patients' Christmas.
excerpt: It is the little from the many that will make Christmas day at the asylum the pleasant oasis of the year

title: Oyster-eating match for a silver cup planned for Christmas
summary: "Van" and "Nitch" were to eat an oyster match for a silver cup on Christmas, billed as the society event of the season.
excerpt: "\"Van\" and \"Nitch\" will eat an oyster match for a silver cup."

title: Territorial supreme court expected to decide Billings–Stark tax case
summary: The supreme court was expected to decide the Billings County tax case some time in February.
excerpt: "This will be done some time in February."

title: Sheep raising to be tried again in the Bad Lands
summary: The paper expected the sheep-raising experiment to be tried again, with at least two flocks to be turned in next spring.
excerpt: at least two flocks will be turned in next spring.
